title: Introduce buddy-style KV block allocator and periodic micro-defrag pass to reduce fragmentation
author: Sofia Martinez
description:
Context and motivation:
The paged KV cache in the runtime has accumulated fragmentation under mixed-length workloads (short chat completions interleaved with long-form generation). This causes >15% memory overhead and occasional 99th-percentile latency spikes during eviction/realloc cycles. Previous attempts (compact-block and slab tuning) mitigated symptoms but not allocator-level fragmentation.

What this PR does:
- Implements a buddy-style allocator for KV cache blocks to reduce internal fragmentation and make coalescing cheaper. The allocator maintains power-of-two size classes up to the page pool size and a lightweight coalescing bitmap for adjacent free blocks.
- Adds per-core local free lists for hot allocations, falling back to global arena to reduce contention under high concurrency.
- Integrates an adaptive micro-defragmentation pass that runs opportunistically during low utilization windows: it looks for adjacent free buddies and merges them; if merging would free a full page, the page is returned to the global pool.
- Introduces pin-token semantics to reduce the cost of temporary pins: short-lived pins use a per-thread fast refcount path; longer pins allocate a durable token object. This reduces atomic ops on the global pin map.
- Provides heuristics to prefer reusing recently-evicted cold blocks when a long allocation is expected (improves reuse locality).
- Adds detailed metrics (kv.buddy.allocs, kv.buddy.coalesces, kv.defrag.cycles, kv.ref_fastpath_hits) and dashboards linked in the PR notes.

Benchmarks and results:
- Microbench: mixed-short/long workload (50/50), 64-concurrency synthetic runner. Memory usage down ~18% at steady-state; allocations/sec slightly improved; tail latencies for allocations down 25% at p99.
- End-to-end: LLM inference throughput for interrupt-heavy chat scenario improved 8% sustained and p99 response time improved by ~12ms on average across runs.

Compatibility and rollout plan:
- New allocator is behind a runtime flag (KV_BUDDY_ALLOC=1) and controlled per-deployment. The default remains the legacy allocator for safety until rollout.
- Migration involves enabling the flag on Dedicated canaries first, then staged rollout with metrics gating (memory-efficiency and allocation-latency).

Files touched (high level):
- service/runtime/kv/buddy_allocator.rs: core allocator implementation and public API.
- service/runtime/kv/block_manager.rs: integration layer, new allocation fastpath and defrag hooks.
- service/runtime/kv/pin_tokens.rs: fastpath refcounting and durable tokens.
- service/runtime/kv/tests/defrag_integration.rs: unit + integration tests for coalescing and forced-defrag scenarios.
- bench/kv_fragmentation_bench.py: reproducible benchmark runner and graphs.
- docs/kv_allocators.md: design notes, flags, and rollout guidance.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for allocator invariants and coalescing logic.
- [x] Integration test verifying cross-thread reuse and pin semantics.
- [x] Bench harness and reproducible results attached.
- [x] Metrics and dashboard tiles added.
- [x] Feature gated behind runtime flag.

Notes on alternatives considered:
- A generalized defragmenter that walks whole cache was rejected due to lock amplification and pause concerns. The buddy approach plus micro-defrag gives a low-latency, incremental path to coalescing.

Risk and mitigation:
- Risk: subtle race in coalescing under concurrent free/alloc. Mitigation: stamp-based validation and double-checked CAS on coalesce; thorough stress tests included.
- Risk: interaction with existing prefix/KV caching heuristics. Mitigation: preserved existing eviction ordering; reuse heuristics only influence allocator placement, not eviction eligibility.

Merge outcome:
- Squash merge to main after approvals and CI green.

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Please add explicit metrics for 'defrag rejected' where coalesce was attempted but failed due to racing allocations. Also add a Prometheus label for deployment_id so we can track by canary.
Sofia Martinez (author): Added kv.defrag.rejected and included deployment_id label on all new metrics. Also added a stress test simulating racing allocations.
Leah Kim: Can you explain the choice of power-of-two max class? Why not hybrid size classes to match observed allocation histogram?

Sofia Martinez (author): We chose power-of-two for cheap buddy arithmetic and simpler coalescing. The micro-defrag pass and reuse heuristics compensate for some internal fragmentation. We benchmarked hybrid schemes but found the extra complexity hurt lock-free fastpaths. Added benchmark results to docs for transparency.
Daniel O'Connor: Found a rare failure in CI stress where defrag pass attempted to coalesce across a page boundary when pool shrink happened. Suggested stamp-based double-check.
Sofia Martinez (author): Implemented stamp validation and CAS retry loop; re-ran stress; passing now.

Arjun Patel: Approved after seeing p99 allocation latency improvements and defensive tests.
Leah Kim: Approved.
Daniel O'Connor: Approved.
release_notes: Introduce an optional buddy-style KV block allocator and incremental micro-defragmentation to reduce fragmentation and tail allocation latency. Feature gated behind KV_BUDDY_ALLOC. Recommended for memory-sensitive workloads. See docs/kv_allocators.md for rollout steps and metrics.
notes:
Flag: KV_BUDDY_ALLOC=1 (runtime)
Dashboards: Infra -> KV Cache -> Buddy Allocator (new)
Rollout: canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% using Linear gating
